title: What is `min.insync.replicas`, and why does it matter alongside `acks=all`?
shortTitle: What is `min.insync.replicas` and why it matters alongside `acks=all`
keyPoints: min.insync.replicas sets the minimum number of in-sync replicas that must persist a record for an acks=all write to succeed.
acks=all alone has a gap: if the ISR shrinks to just the leader, acks=all means acks on one replica.
min.insync.replicas closes this gap by refusing writes when the ISR is too small (NotEnoughReplicas error).
The standard banking config is replication factor 3, min.insync.replicas 2, and acks=all.
This tolerates one broker loss with no data loss and continued writes; two broker losses halt writes to protect data.
min.insync.replicas without acks=all is nearly useless because acks=1 never checks ISR size.
Replication factor must be strictly greater than min.insync.replicas to tolerate a broker failure while still accepting writes.

s1_definition.oneliner: min.insync.replicas sets the minimum replicas that must persist a record for an acks=all write to succeed, so together they guarantee durability by refusing writes that cannot be safely replicated.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **min.insync.replicas** -- a broker and topic configuration that sets the minimum number of in-sync replicas that must acknowledge a write for it to succeed when the producer uses `acks=all`.
- **In-Sync Replica set (ISR)** -- the set of replicas fully caught up with the leader; when a follower falls behind, it leaves the ISR; when it catches up, it rejoins.
- **acks=all** -- the producer waits for every replica in the ISR to persist the record before the broker acknowledges.
- **NotEnoughReplicas** -- the error the broker returns when the ISR drops below min.insync.replicas during an acks=all write.
- **Durability-availability trade-off** -- a higher min.insync.replicas is safer but makes writes unavailable sooner when brokers fail.
- **Standard banking config** -- replication factor 3, min.insync.replicas 2, acks=all: tolerates one broker loss, halts writes on two.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine National Bank of India requires that every important ledger entry be signed by at least two independent officers before it counts as recorded. Setting acks=all is like Rajesh saying I will only consider my transfer done once all on-duty officers have signed. Setting min.insync.replicas to two is the bank's rule that at least two officers must be on duty and signing, otherwise the transaction is refused rather than recorded by a single officer who might go home with the only copy.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  min.insync.replicas + acks=all

  Replication Factor = 3, min.insync.replicas = 2

  Normal (ISR = 3):
  ┌────────┐  ┌────────┐  ┌────────┐
  │Broker 1│  │Broker 2│  │Broker 3│
  │LEADER  │  │follower│  │follower│
  │  ISR   │  │  ISR   │  │  ISR   │
  └────────┘  └────────┘  └────────┘
  Producer write -> all 3 ack -> SUCCESS

  One broker down (ISR = 2):
  ┌────────┐  ┌────────┐  ┌────────┐
  │Broker 1│  │Broker 2│  │Broker 3│
  │LEADER  │  │follower│  │  DOWN  │
  │  ISR   │  │  ISR   │  │        │
  └────────┘  └────────┘  └────────┘
  ISR=2 >= min.isr=2 -> write SUCCESS

  Two brokers down (ISR = 1):
  ┌────────┐  ┌────────┐  ┌────────┐
  │Broker 1│  │Broker 2│  │Broker 3│
  │LEADER  │  │  DOWN  │  │  DOWN  │
  │  ISR   │  │        │  │        │
  └────────┘  └────────┘  └────────┘
  ISR=1 < min.isr=2 -> write REJECTED
  NotEnoughReplicasException
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
min.insync.replicas is the setting that closes the gap in acks=all. With acks=all the producer waits for every replica in the ISR, but if the ISR shrinks to just the leader, acks=all means acks on one, and if that leader fails, an acknowledged record is lost. min.insync.replicas tells the broker the minimum ISR size required for an acks=all write, and if the ISR drops below that number, the broker rejects the write rather than risking data.

The standard safe banking configuration is replication factor 3, min.insync.replicas 2, acks=all. This tolerates one broker loss with no data loss and continued writes. Two broker losses halt writes rather than risking loss, which is the deliberate trade-off of durability over availability.

At National Bank of India, Rajesh once ran transfers with acks=all but min.insync.replicas of 1. During an incident two brokers failed, and when the leader also failed, acknowledged transfers were lost. Pankaj moved to RF=3, min.isr=2, acks=all, so now a single broker loss is tolerated and a two-broker loss halts writes to protect data.

Remember one sentence: acks=all is only as durable as the ISR is deep, and min.insync.replicas guarantees that depth by refusing writes when the ISR is too small.
